items.title: Chillout 101
items.description: Few sounds have become massively popular by stealth quite like chillout did in the '90s and '00s. In many ways a direct precursor to the mood-led state of passive 21st century consumption, the mellowness of downtempo music acts as a bulwark against the rush of modernity. Chillout's supple grooves, cosmopolitan air and typically female vocals became omnipresent in coffee shops, lounges and malls until a backlash slandered the sound as... well, a little too chill. Still, the genre maintains popularity for a reason: we all need a breather now and again. (Cover: Zero 7 / Photo: Rovi)

items.title: Red Hot Chili Peppers Essentials
items.description: Few rock groups of the 1980s broke down as many musical barriers and were as original as the Red Hot Chili Peppers, who evolved from fun-loving party boys to alt-rock elder statesmen over the decades. Perfecting a rousing musical style that combined funk and punk rock (with an explosive stage show to boot), the Chili Peppers spawned a slew of imitators in their wake, but still managed to be the leaders of the pack into the 21st century. Making noise on the Los Angeles scene with early albums such as 1985s ‘Freaky Styley’ and 1989’s ‘Mother's Milk,’ they made a huge breakthrough with 1991’s landmark ‘Blood Sugar Sex Magik,’ a multi-Platinum smash hit that spawned some of their most recognized songs, including “Give It Away” and “Under the Bridge.” That album’s success was bested in 1999 with another catalog peak, the chart-topping ‘Californication,’ which found the band in a more reflective and melodic state. Into the 2000s, they remained fixtures at the top of the international charts with ‘By the Way’ and the double album ‘Stadium Arcadium,’ the latter of which hit No. 1 in almost two dozen countries. While the 2010s were quieter for the group, they still scored Platinum hits with “The Adventures of Rain Dance Maggie,” from 2011’s ‘I’m With You’ and “Dark Necessities” from 2016’s ‘The Getaway.’ In 2022, the Chili Peppers returned with a pair of full-lengths, ‘Unlimited Love’ and ‘Return of the Dream Canteen.’ (Bio: Rovi / Photo: WMG/Press)

items.title: The Chills Essentials
items.description: The early 1980s music scene of Dunedin, New Zealand came to be known as The Dunedin Sound. Characterized by jangly guitars, a lo-fi sound and clever lyrics and championed by the brilliant local label Flying Nun, the university town produced unique bands like The Clean, The Dead C, The Bats – and The Chills. The Chills, formed in 1980 with singer and songwriter Martin Phillips (1963 - 2024) as the only constant member. The Chills enjoyed local stardom and international cult success with early favorites like “Pink Frost”, “Heavenly Pop Hit” and “I Love My Leather Jacket”. Battling different health issues and a constant revolving cast of characters, The Chills rose from the ashes in 2015 with ‘Silver Bullets.’ ‘Snow Bound’ followed in 2018. (Photo: Rovi)

items.title: BHM: 1980s
items.description: At the beginning of the 1980s, many of the music’s most genre-bending superstars were Black. Performers like Prince, Michael Jackson and R&B/soul groups like Earth, Wind & Fire and Rick James were filling arenas and moving units, all of which set the stage for the sound explosion like none other that was born later in the decade in the South Bronx. (Cover: Prince, Getty Images)

items.title: Pablo Chill-E Esenciales
items.description: The Chilean trap star Pablo Chill-E is one of the rising stars out of Latin America, who has received praise from the likes of Anuel AA, Bad Bunny, and Tali Goya. Pablo began making music at the age of 14 and released his viral mixtape 'Antijiles' in 2016. (Photo: Artist's Press)
